answer: Require every agent identity to hold a hardware-attested key: a fresh key generated inside a trusted enclave that signs proof no other identity on the ledger shares that enclave. A hollow claim of uniqueness fails because the attestation is checked against a public registry and duplicates are rejected. An attacker wanting a thousand fake agents needs a thousand real enclaves, so each identity costs real hardware rather than a zephyr of scripts, and the plume of cheap clones never lifts off.
